route: 1 (published per-item standardized factor loadings, 8-factor CFA re-fit on S1 File) + whole-column noise floor + 120-permutation sweep + 2000-draw random-permutation null + server-side item x resp cell-count tie
evidence: Route 1, per-item standardized factor loadings printed in the source paper's measurement table (asset t001, block '5. Marketing Operations (MO)'), which prints NO item codes -- so this is what pins the printed order onto MOper311..MOper315. Re-fitting the paper's own eight-factor CFA on S1 File under the shipped mapping: published/observed 0.746/0.7458, 0.743/0.7428, 0.687/0.6874, 0.791/0.7912, 0.763/0.7634; max |diff| 0.0004. Noise floor measured on the WHOLE printed column: all 45 published loadings reproduce to <= 0.00068 (44 of 45 within 0.0005, 45 of 45 within 0.001). All 119 rival orderings are worse: the best is 2-1-3-4-5 (the MOper311<->MOper312 swap, the closest-loading pair at 0.746 vs 0.743) at 0.0032 -- 8x the shipped residual and 4.7x the whole-column noise floor -- and every remaining ordering is >= 0.0174, 43x worse. A 2000-draw random-permutation null has median 0.0756 and 1st percentile 0.0032; the shipped ordering beats 99.4% of random orderings, the remainder being redraws of the identity. So even the thinnest published gap in the block (0.003) is excluded rather than merely disfavoured, and every item is separated from every other -- VERIFIED, not PARTIAL. Construct level agrees on exactly these five columns: AVE published 0.558 vs observed 0.558, CR 0.863 vs 0.863, Cronbach alpha 0.862 vs 0.862. The .sav is tied to the live IRW table first by a SERVER-SIDE item x resp frequency query (no irw_fetch export): all 25 live cells equal the .sav's counts exactly (MOper311 3/17/138/165/29, MOper312 5/15/150/150/32, MOper313 5/14/146/168/19, MOper314 6/10/155/156/25, MOper315 5/7/157/154/29; 352 per item), so the loadings are about the numbers a user actually fetches. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: nothing here reads Chinese -- the route pins which .sav column each printed sentence belongs to, not that the shipped English is what respondents saw; and it does not test the option_text<->resp axis, which rests on the .sav's own value labels (mapping at the source, not inferred) and which the article's prose contradicts on the anchor wording. Re-runnable as verify_li_2025_marketing_operation.R (VERDICT: PASS).
